effect_size.excerpt: Overall, no significant associations were observed for circulating concentrations of folate (P(trend) = 0.62) or vitamin B(12) (P(trend) = 0.21) with prostate cancer risk. studies.Title: Baseline serum folate, vitamin B12 and the risk of prostate and breast cancer using data from the Swedish AMORIS cohort.
studies.Reference: Baseline serum folate, vitamin B12 and the risk of prostate and breast cancer using data from the Swedish AMORIS cohort.
studies.Population: men in the Swedish AMORIS cohort
studies.comparison_type: Baseline serum vitamin B12; contrast not reported in the abstract

extraction_supporting_text.effect_size: Their associations with PCa and BC risk categories were evaluated using Cox proportional hazards regression. During mean follow-up of 13 years, 703 men developed PCa. There was an inverse association between folate > 32 nmol/L and high-risk PCa [hazard ratio (HR) 0.12, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.02-0.90], and a positive association between folate < 5 nmol/L and metastatic PCa (HR 5.25, 95% CI 1.29-21.41), compared with folate 5-32 nmol/L. No associations with vitamin B12 were found.
extraction_supporting_text.cases: 8,783 men and 19,775 women with vitamin B12 and folate serum measurements were included.
